parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the need for a Rust 2021, std-only Cargo project with /output/test11.rs, exact CLI handling, load-factor logic, and byte-for-byte formatting.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned the project build and verification, then spawned one child named format_probe while continuing implementation; the child independently inspected and patched the shared project.
parallel.implementation: The parent created Cargo.toml, test11.rs, cpp_io, hopscotch_map, table_sizing, and lib modules, fixed a rustc module import, and the child later changed the default max load factor to 0.9 and added tests.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration happened by shared /output side effects: the child modified files in the same project after the parent had already run its own comparison, and the parent delivered the final shared tree.
parallel.verification: The parent ran cargo test, cargo build --release, direct rustc, and sampled binary comparisons; the child also ran cargo tests/builds and a 0..500 comparison sweep before interruption.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official task behavior remained incorrect, but the parent did not receive the child final result and did not perform a parent-side integrated verification after the child's patch.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same Rust 2021, std-only, exact CLI and byte-for-byte output requirements from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned probing, implementation, build, verification, formatting correction, and final delivery without delegation or subagent activity.
serial.implementation: The serial agent inferred the power-of-two bucket policy, created Cargo.toml, test11.rs, load_policy, hopscotch_map, lib, and later formatting modules.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All changes were made in one local sequence; after the formatter patch the same agent rebuilt and delivered the final tree with no cross-agent merge.
serial.verification: The serial agent ran both Cargo and rustc builds, detected float-format mismatches for larger counts, patched formatting, and reran the comparison set with no remaining mismatches.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official task behavior remained incorrect at closure, and the official evaluator passed all 39 testcases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the exact Rust migration, CLI, no-crates, Cargo structure, and byte-for-byte output requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and used the same prompt facts as its acceptance target.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement coverage difference; both official outputs satisfied all 39 testcases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent owned implementation and verification while also spawning /root/format_probe to investigate remaining formatting/behavior details.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent kept all probing, implementation, correction, and verification in one owner.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a parent-child split with shared workspace side effects; serial retained a single sequential owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child inherited the prompt and prior context and worked directly in /output, but its task payload was transferred through an encrypted inter-agent message and no returned result reached the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no inter-agent context boundary; the same actor kept probe findings, implementation decisions, and verification state locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a child boundary and a missing returned handoff, while serial avoided handoff loss by never delegating.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent wrote the initial module layout with a wrong 0.875 default assumption; child later patched the default load factor and tests to 0.9.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial inferred the 0.9 boundary before writing the implementation, then added a formatter after detecting formatting mismatches.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both reached a correct implementation, but parallel corrected a parent-created logic defect through a child patch after parent-side validation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited on the child twice, observed it still running, interrupted it, and finalized without a child final answer.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There was no child result lifecycle; all local findings were immediately available to the same agent before final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an unfinished child handoff at closure, whereas serial had no retrieval or join dependency.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child patched the same /output project after the parent had built and compared its own version, so integration happened through shared filesystem mutation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated changes in one sequence and then rebuilt the exact files it delivered.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's final tree incorporated a child side-effect after parent verification; serial's final tree followed its local patch and rebuild sequence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent comparison passed before the child patch; the child later ran stronger post-patch checks, but that result did not return to the parent before finalization.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial detected formatting mismatches, patched them, rebuilt, and reran the comparison command with no mismatches before finalization.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel passed officially but had stale parent-consumed acceptance evidence; serial had direct post-final-patch acceptance evidence in the same control thread.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used one child, waited through two timeout-style joins, interrupted the child, and completed in 374.929 cell seconds with more token use.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in 252.05 cell seconds with no subagents and no timeout while running the final checks locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent extra lifecycle budget on a child that never returned, but the budget cost did not prevent official success.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both completed current status.json evaluations passed all 39 testcases. The material process difference is that the serial run kept final correction and acceptance in one thread, while the parallel run incorporated a child source patch after the parent had already performed its own integrated comparison and then finalized without a returned child result.
parallel_contributors: The child found a count-57/default-load-factor defect and patched the shared project, which helped the final artifact pass.
The parent's final acceptance narrative was stale because its own comparison pass preceded the child patch and the child never returned a final result.
serial_contributors: The serial agent sampled boundary counts around the default load factor before implementation.
The serial agent patched formatting and reran the final comparison after the last code change.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The parallel parent initially assumed a 0.875 default load factor; the serial run inferred about 0.9 before initial implementation.
The serial run had a formatting mismatch after its first implementation and fixed it locally before final verification.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a realized adverse process issue, not an official failure explanation

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership was present: the parent created the Rust project and the child also performed implementation work in the same tree.
There were not separate component implementations lacking an integrator; the observed issue is timing of a child patch after parent verification.
The parent assembled Cargo.toml, test11.rs, modules, and executable artifacts and delivered them in the final response.
The parent owned the end-to-end implementation, build, comparison, and final response pipeline even though a child later patched shared source.
Implementation was not blocked behind one mandatory preflight; the parent probed, wrote files, built, and verified while the child was active.

The parent did an initial investigation phase, but implementation and later child investigation overlapped enough that no later work was left incomplete or unverified solely by serializing investigation.
No indispensable implementation path lacked capacity; both parent and child produced useful work and the official artifact passed.
The run used one child and did not exhaust the finite task budget; wait overhead did not prevent building, testing, or final delivery.
The child scope expanded into implementation review, but it completed material fixes and checks; no indispensable unfinished work is attributable to an overbroad child assignment.
The child had the full prompt and prior context and produced relevant verification and source changes; no known requirement omitted from the brief made the child work unusable.
No separate interoperating components diverged because of an absent interface contract; the child patched the same simple project rather than producing an incompatible component.
No known finding disappeared through a summary or transfer; the missing child return is a result-lifecycle issue, not lossy transfer of available content.
There was no large returned handoff that the parent failed to reduce; the child did not return a completed handoff before interruption.
No receiver consumed a report describing a superseded workspace state; the stale element was parent verification before a later child patch, retained as merge timing.
No incompatible reports or contracts reached the parent and remained unadjudicated; the child corrected source state rather than returning a conflicting handoff.
The parent did make a final completion claim, but no parent-visible unresolved integrated mismatch remained; the narrower proven problem is a child implementation change after parent verification.
There was no replacement or retry child repeating prior work without inherited checkpoints.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent did interrupt the running child, but the child had already patched and verified the shared project; the distinct retained defect is that the patch landed after parent verification.
A deliverable executable and Cargo project were already placed in /output and finalized; no complete candidate was left unpromoted because finalization began too late.

The parent completed its own comparison and stated the implementation was verified, then the child modified shared source and rebuilt the deliverable; the parent finalized without a returned child result or its own post-child verification.
candidates.realized_consequence: Parent-consumed acceptance evidence no longer covered the delivered shared tree after the child patch, leaving final closure dependent on an unreturned child-side verification rather than a parent post-merge check.
candidates.near_match_reason: The interruption happened in the same lifecycle chain, but the child had already changed the deliverable; correcting the missing post-merge verification is the more specific boundary.

candidates.reason: The child's implementation change was not a completed retrievable result left unjoined; it was already present as a shared-workspace side effect.
The child was not a pure verifier whose concrete finding was trapped below the parent; its source change was already merged, and the retained issue is verification timing.
The child did not fail in a way that left required scope unfinished; the official artifact passed after the child's already-applied patch.
No completed child result was available to the parent and then ignored; the child was interrupted before a final return.

The parent did wait on the child, but it also listed the agent and interrupted it after local verification; the adverse issue is post-verification child modification, not blind waiting until task deadline.
There were no competing cross-file designs claiming incompatible behavior; the child patched the same implementation path to correct it.
Parent and child edited overlapping source files, but no same-file conflict or reconciliation failure is shown; the concrete consequence is the later merge after parent verification.
The child patched constants and tests rather than deleting, recreating, or wholesale rewriting another actor's non-entry source module.
The child rebuilt /output/test11, but this deliverable update is part of the same post-verification merge chain and did not independently replace a needed submitted artifact with a conflicting one.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion that replaced multiple final outputs and invalidated another final-tree contribution.
The agents shared /output, but the more specific observed problem is the child patch landing after parent verification; shared workspace alone is not enough.
No generated artifact, temporary fixture, cache, or auxiliary implementation from one actor was consumed by another as a reference environment.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Early Child Termination rejected for the same child lifecycle because the patch-after-parent-verification boundary is more specific.
Deliverable Overwrite and Same-File Collision rejected for the same shared-workspace chain because no independent conflicting overwrite consequence appeared.
Missing Verifier Return rejected because the child did not return, but the concrete issue is the unclosed post-merge verification loop.
